To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and sequenced the first cDNA clone for the chlorophyll synthesis pathway in Euglena gracilis, that we have shown that the enzyme is synthesised with an unusually long N-terminal extension, and that we have shown the sequence to be 60-70 per cent similar to that of the human erythrocyte and E. coli enzymes.
the cDNA clone for hydroxymethylbile synthase (HMS) from Euglena gracillis has been isolated.
we have isolated and characterized the cDNA for hydroxymethyl bilane synthase, an enzyme in the porphyin pathway, from Euglena gracillis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of chlorophyll in the chloroplast of the unicellular green alga Euglena gracilis.
the isolation, characterisation, and expression of genes involved in chlorophyll synthesis in Euglena gracilis, a unicellular green alga.

the isolation and characterisation of genes involved in the synthesis of chlorophyll in the unicellular green alga Euglena gracilis and with their expression during the cell's adaptation to light and shade conditions.

this is the first report of a transit peptide sequence for a chloroplast enzyme encoded by a nuclear gene in Euglena.
this cDNA clone encodes a protein with a very long N-terminal extension that is probably a chloroplast transit peptide.

the transit peptide of the chloroplast enzyme is very different in sequence from those of other chloroplast proteins.
a cDNA clone has been isolated and characterised for the chloroplast enzyme hydroxy-methylbilane synthetase from Euglena.
we have cloned a cDNA encoding the complete sequence of a chlorophyll biosynthesis enzyme, hydroxymethyl-bilane synthase.

the transit peptides of nuclear-encoded chloroplast proteins can be quite long and complex.
